facts.text: On this day in 1945, the Nuremberg trials opened — the first time in history that leaders of a defeated nation were held criminally accountable under international law, setting the precedent for every war crimes tribunal that followed.
On this day in 1917, British tanks massed at Cambrai for the first large-scale tank assault in history, advancing further in hours than months of Somme fighting had achieved.
Mongolia has more horses than people — roughly 4.3 million horses to 3.4 million humans — and a significant portion of the population still navigates the steppe on horseback rather than by road.

The Philippines is the only country in the world where divorce remains entirely illegal for most of its citizens, with annulment the sole legal exit from marriage and cases routinely taking a decade to resolve.
Jakarta is sinking so fast — up to 25 centimeters per year in some districts — that Indonesia has already begun relocating its capital to a new city, Nusantara, carved from Borneo jungle.
On this date in 1992, Queen Elizabeth II offered to pay income tax voluntarily — markets barely blinked, but Buckingham Palace's finances have been publicly scrutinized ever since.
On Nov 20, 1945, the Nuremberg trials opened. IG Farben, the chemical conglomerate that supplied Zyklon B, was not dissolved until 2012.

The New York Stock Exchange was founded in 1792 under a buttonwood tree. The original 24 brokers agreed to charge each other a minimum commission — the first recorded price-fixing cartel in American finance.
Saudi Aramco briefly hit a $2 trillion market cap in 2019, making it worth more than Google, Amazon, and Facebook combined at the time.
Japan's Nikkei 225 peaked on December 29, 1989 and took 35 years to reclaim that high — the longest index recovery in modern market history.

On this date in 1998, the first module of the International Space Station launched — a structure now so large it covers more area than a football field, orbiting at 28,000 km/h close enough to see with the naked eye.
Your femur withstands forces up to five times your body weight while walking. Running triples that. It is, pound for pound, stronger than concrete.
On this date in 1789, New Jersey became the first U.S. state to ratify the Bill of Rights — but that is history. In science: the carbon in those ink molecules is older than the solar system.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A teaspoon of its material would weigh roughly a billion tons on Earth.
The human eye can detect a single photon of light in complete darkness. Your visual system is operating at the absolute physical limit of sensitivity.
On this day in 1945, the Nuremberg trials opened — making their verdicts younger than the first McDonald's franchise, which opened in 1953.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. The pyramid is simply that old.
On this day in 1789, New Jersey became the first state to ratify the Bill of Rights — three years before Kentucky even existed as a state.
The fax machine was invented in 1843, before anyone had laid a single mile of US transcontinental railroad track. We did not upgrade eagerly.
Oxford University was already 200 years old when the Aztec Empire was founded. It is still operating. The Aztec Empire is not.
Saudade (Portuguese): a melancholic longing for something beloved that may never return. Linguists consider it untranslatable — English requires an entire sentence to approximate one word.
Apricity: the warmth of winter sun on your skin. The word existed in 1623 and then, inexplicably, fell out of use. It deserves to be brought back.
On this day in 1820, the Essex was rammed by a sperm whale — the real event that inspired Moby-Dick. The crew survived 90 days at sea; Melville called it 'the most extraordinary' story he ever heard.
Hiraeth (Welsh): a homesickness for a home you cannot return to, or one that never existed. It carries grief, longing, and belonging simultaneously — three emotions English treats as unrelated.
On this day in 1945, the Nuremberg trials opened. The word 'genocide' had been coined just one year earlier by Raphael Lemkin, who spent years lobbying for the very tribunal that now used his term.

On this date in 2017, Bitcoin hit $8,000 for the first time — then doubled again within three weeks. The entire move happened with no ETFs, no institutional custody rails, and Coinbase crashing under load.

On this date in 2021, El Salvador's Bitcoin bonds ('Volcano Bonds') were formally announced by President Bukele at a Bitcoin conference in El Salvador — they finally launched in January 2025 after three years of regulatory delays.

The Bitcoin genesis block contains the text 'Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks' — Satoshi embedded a Times headline dated Jan 3, 2009, making the block's timestamp independently verifiable via newspaper archive.

Ethereum's EIP-1559, live since August 2021, has permanently destroyed over 4.4 million ETH in base fees. The burn mechanism means Ethereum's monetary policy is set by transaction demand, not a fixed schedule.

The DAO hack in 2016 drained 3.6 million ETH through a reentrancy bug — but the attacker couldn't move the funds for 28 days due to a lockup in their own exploit contract, giving Ethereum time to execute the controversial hard fork.

On this date in 2022, ChatGPT launched publicly. It reached 1 million users in 5 days — faster than any consumer product in history — and forced every major tech company to accelerate AI roadmaps by years.

On this date in 2019, OpenAI released the full GPT-2 model it had withheld for 9 months over misuse fears. The cautious release was later widely considered unnecessary; no significant misuse materialized.
AlphaFold2 predicted structures for over 200 million proteins — essentially the entire known proteome — in 2022. Structural biologists had expected that work to take centuries at experimental pace.
The training run for GPT-4 is estimated to have consumed roughly 50 gigawatt-hours of electricity. That is comparable to the annual consumption of about 4,500 average US households, spent in weeks.
RLHF — reinforcement learning from human feedback — was not invented by OpenAI. The core technique dates to a 2017 DeepMind and OpenAI joint paper on learning reward functions from human preferences.
